se-abjure-1.explanation: An oath sworn in open court is a formal giving up of a claim, which is what abjure and repudiate both say; hedging or delimiting a claim would leave it standing.
se-abjure-1.stem: Standing before the tribunal, the exiled minister agreed to _____ every claim he had ever made to the throne, on oath and in front of the court.

se-bucolic-1.explanation: Hayricks and lanes with no trace of the modern world is an idealised countryside, which bucolic and pastoral both name; quotidian and prosaic would make it ordinary rather than rural.
se-bucolic-1.stem: The paintings sold well in the city precisely because the England they showed was _____: hayricks, lanes, and nothing that had happened since 1890.

se-diatribe-1.explanation: Forty minutes of attack on a hiring record is a sustained verbal assault, which diatribe and harangue both name; a eulogy or panegyric would be praise instead.
se-diatribe-1.stem: What the committee had scheduled as a brief status report became a forty-minute _____ against the department's entire hiring record.

se-ebullient-1.explanation: Telling strangers on a train about a job he has not been offered is uncontainable high spirits, which is what ebullient and exuberant say; serene and morose are the quiet ends of the scale.
se-ebullient-1.stem: He came back from the interview so _____ that he told three strangers on the train he had got the job before the offer had been made.

se-hackneyed-1.explanation: Phrases used a thousand times that the audience can predict are worn out from repetition, which is what hackneyed and trite both mean; the rest describe fussiness, haste or calm.
se-hackneyed-1.stem: Every image in the speech had been used a thousand times before, and the audience could hear the _____ phrases coming a full sentence ahead.

se-intransigent-1.explanation: A fortnight of mediation that moves nobody describes a refusal to budge, which intransigent and obdurate both carry; erratic would mean the position kept changing.
se-intransigent-1.stem: Two mediators and a fortnight of talks left the union exactly where it had started, _____ on every point that the company cared about.

se-meticulous-1.explanation: Recording every variable for every trial is extreme care over detail, which meticulous and punctilious both name; cursory and token say the opposite and erratic says something else again.
se-meticulous-1.stem: Her notebooks recorded the temperature, the time and the observer for every single trial, a habit so _____ that it rescued the study years later.

se-mollify-1.explanation: The customers are angry and the apology is meant to calm them, which is what mollify and propitiate do; provoke is the opposite and the other options do nothing to a person's temper.
se-mollify-1.stem: A written apology and a partial refund did little to _____ customers who had already spent most of a Saturday on hold.

se-munificent-1.explanation: One bequest paying for an entire wing is giving on a grand scale, which munificent and lavish both say; miserly and stingy are its opposite.
se-munificent-1.stem: The new wing was paid for by a single _____ bequest from a former student who had never once come back for a reunion.

se-perfunctory-1.explanation: Four minutes and a single tick is going through the motions, which perfunctory and cursory both describe; thorough is the opposite of what the sentence reports.
se-perfunctory-1.stem: The inspection lasted four minutes and produced one tick in one box; the whole exercise was _____ and satisfied nobody who had asked for it.

se-prevaricate-1.explanation: Answers that could be read two ways and commit him to nothing are evasion rather than denial, which is what prevaricate and equivocate name; to recant or rebut he would have had to say something definite.
se-prevaricate-1.stem: Asked three times where the money had gone, the treasurer continued to _____, offering answers that could be read two ways and committed him to neither.

se-refute-1.explanation: Publishing evidence against a suggestion is disproving it, which refute and rebut both say; to recant or forswear you would have to be abandoning your own position instead.
se-refute-1.stem: The replication data was published precisely to _____ the suggestion that the original effect had been an artefact of one faulty machine.

tc-aesthetic-1.explanation: The sentence sets function against appearance and says the complaint was about the eyesore, so the objections were aesthetic, concerned with how it looks.
tc-aesthetic-1.stem: The objections to the new bridge were entirely _____: nobody doubted that it would carry the traffic, only that it would be an eyesore for a century.

tc-avarice-1.explanation: Three heirs each grasping for the whole estate and refusing to sell is greed, which avarice names; apathy or deference would have settled it in an afternoon.
tc-avarice-1.stem: The estate was broken up not by debt but by _____: three heirs who each wanted the land and none of whom would sell to the others.

tc-conspicuous-1.explanation: A yellow coat among grey ones attracts every eye, and the wish to attend quietly is the contrast: conspicuous means plainly noticeable, where furtive and covert mean hidden.
tc-conspicuous-1.stem: In a room where everyone else wore grey, the yellow coat made her the most _____ person at a meeting she had hoped to attend quietly.

tc-contentious-1.explanation: Four hours of comment and a walkout is an item that provokes argument, which contentious names; anodyne and innocuous would mean nobody minded.
tc-contentious-1.stem: The zoning amendment proved the most _____ item on the agenda: four hours of public comment and two councillors walking out.

tc-convoluted-1.explanation: Nine cross-referring clauses that nobody can explain is complexity nobody can follow, which convoluted names; pellucid and limpid claim the opposite.
tc-convoluted-1.stem: The refund policy runs to nine clauses, each referring to two others, and no clerk in the shop could explain the _____ result.

tc-decorum-1.explanation: Holding his bearing in court despite what he felt is dignified, proper conduct: decorum. Levity and effrontery would be the breaches his supporters wanted.
tc-decorum-1.stem: Whatever he felt about the ruling, he maintained the _____ expected in a courtroom, which his own supporters outside found infuriating.

tc-delineate-1.explanation: Nine pages of coordinates fixing which waters belong to whom is a precise description of boundaries, which is what delineate does.
tc-delineate-1.stem: The opening article of the treaty exists to _____ exactly which waters each fleet may enter, and it runs to nine pages of coordinates.

tc-derivative-1.explanation: Gestures borrowed from other operas is the clue: derivative means copied rather than original, and novel and inimitable would praise the very quality it lacks.
tc-derivative-1.stem: Critics allowed that the staging was handsome but called the score _____, a careful assembly of gestures borrowed from three better operas.

tc-didactic-1.explanation: Characters who abandon the story to lecture the reader have turned the book into instruction, which is what didactic means; pedantic would be fussiness over small details.
tc-didactic-1.stem: The novel's early chapters tell a story; the last fifty pages turn so _____ that the characters stop speaking to each other and begin lecturing the reader.

tc-diffident-1.explanation: Apologising for her own presence despite doing the best work is a lack of confidence rather than an unwillingness to speak, which is what diffident names and reticent does not.
tc-diffident-1.stem: She had done the best work in the department and still introduced herself as though apologising for the interruption, and no amount of praise made her less _____.

tc-dilettante-1.explanation: Four fields dabbled in and none mastered is the dabbler without serious commitment that dilettante names; a virtuoso would have mastered at least one.
tc-dilettante-1.stem: He had published one paper in each of four fields and mastered none of them, and the review summed him up in a single word: _____.

tc-disabuse-1.explanation: Freeing a person of a mistaken belief they hold is disabuse; debunk is done to the claim itself rather than to the new arrival who holds it.
tc-disabuse-1.stem: It fell to the ward sister to _____ every new arrival of the idea that the night shift would be a quiet one.

tc-disingenuous-1.explanation: Pleading surprise while holding a month-old draft is insincerity dressed as frankness, which disingenuous names; candid and artless would make the claim honest.
tc-disingenuous-1.stem: His claim to have been taken by surprise was _____: the emails show he had drafted the announcement a month before the vote.

tc-disparate-1.explanation: Three kinds of art with nothing in common in one room is the clue: disparate means fundamentally unalike, where homogeneous and analogous claim likeness.
tc-disparate-1.stem: The exhibition asks a great deal of its visitors, hanging Flemish portraits beside protest photography and vending-machine art in one _____ room.

tc-dissemble-1.explanation: Making a terrifying hand look like a boring one is hiding what you actually feel, which is what dissemble means; hedging would be avoiding a commitment instead.
tc-dissemble-1.stem: A good player has to _____ at the table: the hand that terrifies him must look exactly like the hand that bores him.

tc-disseminate-1.explanation: Not suppressed but kept inside three departments is a refusal to spread it widely, which is what disseminate means; expurgate and occlude describe other kinds of burial.
tc-disseminate-1.stem: The ministry's own study was never suppressed; officials simply declined to _____ it beyond the three departments that had commissioned the work.

tc-dupe-1.explanation: A scheme that works by looking harmless is built to deceive, which dupe says; apprise and disabuse would mean telling the victims the truth instead.
tc-dupe-1.stem: The scheme worked because it was dull: nothing about a quarterly statement full of small steady gains looks designed to _____ anyone.

tc-emulate-1.explanation: Copying the teacher's practice in the hope of eventually surpassing her is exactly what emulate means, as against merely reacting to or avoiding her.
tc-emulate-1.stem: Every young cellist in the class hoped to _____ her teacher, practising the same passages for hours in the hope of one day playing them better.

tc-endemic-1.explanation: Fifteen years of audits finding the same thing sets it against occasional lapses: endemic means regularly found in that place, where transient and anomalous say passing or rare.
tc-endemic-1.stem: Delays of this kind are not occasional lapses in the ministry; they are _____, and every audit for fifteen years has said so.

tc-erudite-1.explanation: Nine languages in footnotes longer than the text is a display of deep and wide learning, which is what erudite means; cursory and indolent describe the opposite effort.
tc-erudite-1.stem: The footnotes ran longer than the chapters and quoted nine languages, which made the book _____ enough to impress reviewers and defeat most of its readers.

tc-eschew-1.explanation: A monastic rule enforced by the abbot requires deliberate abstention from the three comforts listed, which is what eschew means; countenance would be permitting them.
tc-eschew-1.stem: The rule of the order required its members to _____ meat, wine and soft bedding, and the abbot enforced all three without exception.

tc-exonerate-1.explanation: Naming the real author clears the men punished in his place, which is what exonerate means; impugn and castigate would blame them further.
tc-exonerate-1.stem: The second inquiry did what the first refused to do: it named the ledger's true author and went on to _____ the two clerks dismissed in 1994.

tc-fortuitous-1.explanation: A plate left by a window by accident, producing the mould that became a drug, is luck rather than design, and fortuitous is the word for it; inexorable would make it inevitable.
tc-fortuitous-1.stem: The discovery was entirely _____: a technician left a culture plate beside an open window and came back to find the mould that became the drug.

tc-furtive-1.explanation: Glancing at the door and hiding an envelope is stealthy behaviour that gives itself away, which is what furtive describes; ostentatious would mean he wanted to be seen.
tc-furtive-1.stem: He kept glancing at the door and sliding the envelope under a magazine, and the more _____ he looked the more certain the table became that something was being hidden.

tc-gainsay-1.explanation: Figures drawn from the company's own filings are hard to contradict, and gainsay is the word for the denial the critics did not attempt.
tc-gainsay-1.stem: The figures came from the company's own filings, and not even its fiercest critics attempted to _____ them.

tc-gregarious-1.explanation: Three dinner invitations per market walk is sociability, which gregarious names; insular, retiring and diffident all describe someone who avoids company.
tc-gregarious-1.stem: Field notes describe him as _____ to a fault: he could not walk the length of the market without acquiring three dinner invitations.

tc-intrepid-1.explanation: Attempting a crossing that defeats most parties takes fearlessness: intrepid. The other four all describe the caution or cowardice that would keep a surveyor away.
tc-intrepid-1.stem: The eastern ridge in November defeats most parties, and only the most _____ surveyors attempt the crossing at all.

tc-inundate-1.explanation: Eleven thousand messages into a two-person office is a flood, which inundate names; parry and forestall would mean the office fended the wave off.
tc-inundate-1.stem: One television mention was enough to _____ a two-person office with eleven thousand messages over a single weekend.

tc-irresolute-1.explanation: Asking for extensions until the offers lapse is an inability to decide, which irresolute names; steadfast and resolute would describe the opposite failing.
tc-irresolute-1.stem: Faced with two acceptable offers and a firm deadline, he proved _____, asking for extensions until both had been withdrawn.

tc-maverick-1.explanation: Questioning every assumption is the opposite of the safe hands the board wanted: a maverick is the independent nonconformist, where a sycophant would flatter instead.
tc-maverick-1.stem: The board wanted a safe pair of hands and got the _____ of the department, who spent his first month questioning every assumption in the strategy.

tc-obstinate-1.explanation: Nine months of identical refusals is a refusal to move at all, which obstinate names; amenable, docile and tractable all describe someone who would have bent.
tc-obstinate-1.stem: Every concession was refused in the same three lines, and after nine months the mediator described the landlord as simply _____.

tc-ostentatious-1.explanation: Marble, fountains and an unused helipad are display for its own sake, which ostentatious names; understated and frugal describe the restraint the clients wanted.
tc-ostentatious-1.stem: The new headquarters is _____ in a way the firm's own clients found alarming: a marble atrium, two fountains and a helipad nobody uses.

tc-presumptuous-1.explanation: Advising on a funeral after two meetings is overstepping what the acquaintance allows, which presumptuous names; deferential and diffident would mean holding back.
tc-presumptuous-1.stem: It struck the family as _____ of a neighbour they had met twice to offer firm advice about the funeral arrangements.

tc-relegate-1.explanation: Introduction to small-type appendix is a demotion, which relegate names; exalt, aggrandize and anoint would all move the chapter the other way.
tc-relegate-1.stem: The second edition moved her chapter out of the introduction and chose to _____ it to an appendix printed in smaller type.

tc-stolid-1.explanation: The blank expression held for six weeks under a sentence is the clue: stolid names that unmoved, emotionless bearing, while the other options all require visible feeling.
tc-stolid-1.stem: Witnesses expected the defendant to flinch when the sentence was read, but he remained _____, wearing the same blank expression he had for six weeks.

tc-supplant-1.explanation: The sentence rules out assisting, so the sensors take the method's place entirely, which supplant means; augment and perpetuate would leave it standing.
tc-supplant-1.stem: Cheap sensors did not merely assist the old survey method; within five years they had begun to _____ it in every commercial practice.

tc-taciturn-1.explanation: Three conversations in ten years, and silence even at his own party, describes a habit of saying very little, which is exactly taciturn; the rest describe talkers.
tc-taciturn-1.stem: Colleagues who had worked beside him for a decade could recall perhaps three conversations; he was _____ even at his own retirement party.

tc-venerate-1.explanation: A statue and an endowed lecture are acts of deep respect, which venerate names, and they reverse the vilifying the town once did.
tc-venerate-1.stem: Two centuries after the trial, the town that drove him out has put up a statue and endowed a lecture in order to _____ him.
